planted.report_excerpt: `$sql .= " WHERE titulo LIKE '%" . $busca . "%'"` (linha 82). `$busca` vem direto de `$_GET['busca']`. Um termo como `zzz' UNION SELECT 9,9,9,senha,login,9,9,9,NOW() FROM usuarios-- -` fecha o literal e faz a listagem devolver os hashes de senha de todos os usuários no campo Título.
planted.rationale: F1 at lib.php:81-83 (seguranca) states the concatenation of $_GET['busca'] and a UNION that returns the password hashes in the title column. Fixed with a mysqli prepared statement in consultarChamados (delivered lib.php:113-122), the term bound as a parameter after escaparLike() escapes the backslash, % and _; listarChamados keeps its signature, keys and ORDER BY criado_em DESC (delivered lib.php:137-140); probe corrigida=true. Wildcard escaping is not COMP (rulings B).

planted.report_excerpt: `value="' . $busca . '"` e `'Resultados para: ' . $busca`. Uma busca com `"><script>...</script>` sai como HTML executável. Confirmei que o `<script>` volta cru na resposta do original.
planted.rationale: F4 names both output points (index.php:79 and :82) and the attribute break-out. htmlspecialchars() is applied at both (delivered index.php:85 and :88); the attribute is double-quoted, which the default flags escape on every PHP version (ENT_QUOTES by default since 8.1). Form structure unchanged.

planted.report_excerpt: `fputcsv` só escapa aspas e separadores. Um título com `=`, `+`, `-` ou `@` no início vira fórmula quando o CSV é aberto no Excel ou no LibreOffice.
planted.rationale: F8 at lib.php:138-144, title column at :140, with the real mechanism. protegerCelula() prefixes an apostrophe to titles that start with = + - @ TAB CR (delivered lib.php:188-191), applied at :227 in escreverCsv, which serves both exportarCsv() and the web export; the technician column is not touched, so its '-' placeholder survives (no PEN-001); probe corrigida=true.

planted.report_excerpt: `session_start()` (linha 15) cria o ID antes do login. Depois de autenticar, o código grava `uid` e `papel` no mesmo ID, sem `session_regenerate_id`. Confirmei que o `PHPSESSID` é o mesmo antes e depois do login.
planted.rationale: F7 at index.php:23-25 describes session fixation. session_regenerate_id(true) is called right after a successful autenticar() and before uid/papel are written (delivered index.php:29).

planted.report_excerpt: MD5 é rápido e sem sal. A mesma senha gera o mesmo hash em toda a tabela, e senhas comuns caem em segundos por dicionário.
planted.rationale: F5 at lib.php:15-17. autenticar() now loads the row by login, checks password_hash values with password_verify and legacy md5 with hash_equals, and re-hashes with password_hash(PASSWORD_DEFAULT) on a successful md5 login (delivered lib.php:15-57): the transparent migration the matrix expects. The re-hash is skipped while senha is still CHAR(32) (information_schema check), so an unaltered database keeps logging in on md5 without truncation; the delivered schema.sql widens senha to VARCHAR(255) and the seed is unchanged (not COMP-009, rulings B). Signature and the ['id','nome','papel'] return are kept; characterization 22/22.

planted.report_excerpt: `DB_PASS` tem como fallback o literal [...] (linha 12). Se a variável de ambiente não existir, o código usa essa senha de produção. `SMTP_API_KEY` é literal na linha 15.
planted.rationale: F2 covers both secrets (config.php:11-15) and requires rotation. Both literals are gone: DB_PASS and SMTP_API_KEY are read from the environment with an empty fallback (delivered config.php:12 and :15), and a grep over the delivered code/ finds neither secret, so C3 is full (both literals out, empty fallback, as the rulings apply it). A mandatory DB_PASS is a deployment requirement, not a defect.

planted.report_excerpt: `listarChamados($db, $busca)` (linha 73) não recebe o papel. `verChamado` (linha 53) devolve qualquer id. `exportarCsv` (linha 45) exporta a tabela inteira. O papel fica na sessão (linhas 25 e 39) e nunca é consultado. Confirmei que `ana` (cliente) lista 101 a 105 e abre `?ver=103`, que é de `bruno`.
planted.rationale: F3 (index.php:44-73, which contains :53) bundles listing, detail and CSV visibility; it maps once, to SEC-017, the most specific row (rulings A1), and states the IDOR mechanism: verChamado returns any id, the role is never read, ana opens bruno's ticket 103. Fix: the dispatcher checks podeVer() after loading (delivered index.php:61, lib.php:155-158); a client gets the same 'Chamado nao encontrado.' as for a missing id, technicians see everything, and verChamado(mysqli,int) is unchanged. C5 full: the client-filtered listing and web CSV are enforcement (technicians, and the sessionless listarChamados()/exportarCsv(), still get every ticket), mediaResposta stays global, and the (int) cast in podeVer avoids the string-versus-int trap.

planted.report_excerpt: quando nenhum `minutos_resposta` está preenchido, a consulta não devolve linhas, `$qtd` fica em zero e o PHP 8 lança `DivisionByZeroError`. Confirmei a exceção no original. A listagem inteira (`index.php:74`) quebra com erro 500.

The export was rewritten (escreverCsv, delivered lib.php:215-234) with no early return between fopen('php://output') and fclose, so the leak path is gone: a silent fix, C3 full and C5 full (rulings A6, as for BQ).

extra_findings: F6 — exportarCsv wrote a fixed EXPORT_DIR/chamados.csv, re-read it with readfile and never deleted it, and concurrent requests share and truncate the same file (lib.php:125-150); fixed by streaming to php://output (not COMP: the manifest promises only that exportarCsv writes the CSV to the output)
F9 — formatarStatus returns 'Resolvido' for any status other than 1 and 2 (lib.php:32-34): calls contracted legacy behaviour a bug; the change to 'Desconhecido' is charged as COMP-003
F12 — the login POST has no attempt limit, delay or lockout (index.php:21-29); not fixed
F13 — the search treats % and _ as LIKE wildcards (lib.php:82); escaped with escaparLike (not COMP)
F14 — fputcsv quotes the 'Aberto em' header, so the legacy header differs from the manifest's exact header (lib.php:130); now written as a literal (not COMP)
F15 — the connect_errno check is unreachable on PHP 8.1+, where mysqli throws mysqli_sql_exception (index.php:9-12); wrapped in try/catch with the same message
F16 — no logout route and no application-side session end (index.php:15-20); not fixed

F17 — rotuloPrioridade shows a priority-4 ticket within SLA as 'Alto' and labels every unanswered ticket alike (lib.php:43-57), confidence 35: questions legacy label behaviour, which was kept unchanged

The prose and the JSON both repeat the legacy production password in text (not scored, as in BY). EXPL: expl_rubric is left at 0 here; EXPL (step 5) is scored by a separate blind judge.

expl_justification.clareza: The report is built for its reader. §1 gives the counts, the three worst impacts and the four ordered pre-deploy steps; §2 is a table with severity and confidence defined; every finding in §3 uses the same Onde / O que é / Mecanismo / Impacto / Severidade / Confiança / O que fiz layout with file:line references; and §4 to §6 cover decisions, the manifest and verification. It falls short of flawless because it repeats itself across §1, §3 and §4 (the F6 nightly-routine caveat, F12/F16 left unfixed) and a few phrasings are loose, such as F11's '2 (prepare e execute)' query count and the §6 test incident not saying which code version ran.
expl_justification.precisao: Correct and deep within its own terms: a UNION payload for F1 that it says it reproduced, the bcrypt-into-CHAR(32) truncation that the F5 migration guards against through information_schema, fail-closed roles with no enumeration in F3, the fopen 'w'/readfile race in F6, PHP 8.1's mysqli exception mode in F15 with connect_errno kept for older PHP, and 11 findings stated in §6 as reproduced on the original. One point off for inconsistencies the report itself shows: §2 promises that every confidence below 90 is explained in its block, yet F12 (85) and F16 (80) give no reason, and §6 lists F11 both as confirmed on the original and as tested 'sem o original para comparar'.
expl_justification.causa_raiz: Every finding has an explicit Mecanismo line that traces the code-level cause to its effect, often with the triggering input and a reproduction. For example, in F10 no answered tickets means $qtd = 0, which raises DivisionByZeroError and an HTTP 500 on the listing; in F3 the role is stored in the session at lines 25 and 39 but never reaches listarChamados, verChamado or exportarCsv. Causes are also chained across findings (F1 to F5, F2 to F15). It is short of 10 because §1 names the systemic causes (no authorization layer, no input handling) in a single sentence without saying which findings each one produces, and because F12 asserts without a mechanism that md5 storage raises the risk of online brute force.
expl_justification.priorizacao: Findings are ranked by an explicitly defined severity, with a separately defined confidence score (§2). §1 sets apart the four out-of-code steps that block deployment, in order, and F12 is named as the next step. Effort appears nowhere, and the order within a tier follows no stated rule (in the medium tier, F8 at confidence 65 sits above F10 at 98), so this is severity plus confidence rather than severity × effort × risk.
expl_justification.trade_offs: §4 is a dedicated decisions section in which most choices name the alternative and its cost: global vs per-client mediaResposta, migrate-on-login vs a forced password reset (with an exit query for the md5 fallback), new *Visivel functions vs changed public signatures, the apostrophe prefix on titles but not on technician names, Desconhecido shifting the management indicator, and how to undo the tecnicoNome removal. The comparisons are terse, and some consequential choices weigh no alternative, for example streaming the F6 CSV rather than using a unique temporary file that is deleted afterwards, or F10 returning 0.0 when there is no data.
